quotes.text: Too many makers assume a clean answer in testing equals mission accomplished. In reality, that's just story mode on easy difficulty.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Warns that a successful demo says little about production readiness.

quotes.text: If you treat those four pieces as detached silos, the whole tower wobbles. A solid skill without grounding is just a fancy hallucination.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains why model, orchestration, grounding and skills must be designed as one stack.

quotes.text: End users see the same prompt box and answer card whether you build the agent in studio or with toolkit. That's by design, the UX layer is unified.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clarifies that the tool choice is operational, not about the user interface.

quotes.text: Grounding isn't an advanced bonus feature. It's the baseline that separates useful copilots from untrustworthy chatterboxes.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Positions grounding as the foundation of trustworthy agents.

quotes.text: The practical rule is that teams Toolkit hides costs in integration and service layers, where studio makes you pay upfront in credits. Neither is cheaper.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Gives a clear rule of thumb for comparing the cost models.

chapters.title: Why the demo is not the boss fight

takeaways: Choose Copilot Studio for fast low-code agents within Microsoft's guardrails and the Teams Toolkit (Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit) for custom orchestration and deep integration.
Agents need grounding in enterprise sources with sensitivity labels and Purview classification, otherwise they either invent answers or expose data.
Governance and cost control, from admin roles and diagnostic logs to Copilot credit monitoring and budget alerts, must be in place before an agent goes to production.
hook: Building a Copilot agent that works in a demo is easy; keeping it reliable, compliant and affordable in production is not. This episode is for makers, developers and admins deciding between Copilot Studio and the Teams Toolkit. It covers architecture, grounding, governance and licensing so your agents survive real-world load.
